turnout_basis: votes cast (incl. informal and disallowed) as % of enrolled electors

parties.name: National
parties.note: Official count gave 48 seats (43 electorate + 5 list). Winning the Port Waikato by-election (25 Nov 2023) added a 49th seat (an extra overhang seat): 44 electorate + 5 list.

government.name: Sixth National Government
government.notes: First three-party coalition under MMP. Separate coalition agreements National–ACT and National–NZ First were signed on 24 Nov 2023; ministers sworn in 27 Nov 2023. Deputy PM rotates: Winston Peters (NZ First) to 31 May 2025, then David Seymour (ACT). Government holds 68 of 123 seats (49+11+8) after the Port Waikato by-election.

electorates.name: Port Waikato
electorates.note: Electorate vote cancelled at the general election after the death of ACT candidate Neil Christensen; filled at the 2023 Port Waikato by-election, 25 Nov 2023 (turnout c. 35.7%). Majority per RNZ final results.

notes: Electorate majorities/runners-up are taken from the official-count vote tables in each electorate's Wikipedia article (which cite the Electoral Commission's official results pages); where the summary table, the article's majority box and the candidate vote counts disagree, the value two of them agree on is used – see 'majority_corrections'.

Official results (3 Nov 2023) were adjusted by judicial recounts later in Nov 2023; figures here follow the post-recount table on Wikipedia (e.g. National 1,085,851 / 38.08%). Some contemporaneous reports quote the pre-recount 1,085,016 / 38.06%.
Te Pāti Māori won 6 electorates but its 3.08% party vote entitled it to 4 seats: 2 overhang seats (122). Port Waikato by-election added a third overhang seat (123).

Cross-check: national party-vote totals vs the sum of per-electorate official party votes in the electorate articles – largest gap -1003 votes (green, 0.04% of valid votes); gaps are attributed to transcription errors in individual electorate articles, and the national (Electoral Commission summary) figures are used.
